title: Reporting statements: that-clauses
subtitle: He said (that) he was enjoying his work.
summary: Report statements with a that-clause: know when that can be left out, which verbs need an object first, and which need a preposition before that object.

lesson.heading: Leaving out that
lesson.text: After common reporting verbs such as agree, mention, notice, promise, say and think we often leave **that** out, especially in informal speech. We usually keep it after less common verbs (complain, confide, deny, grumble, speculate, warn - and answer, argue, reply), in formal writing, and whenever the that-clause does not come immediately after the verb.

examples.text: He said (**that**) he was enjoying his work.
The members of the Security Council warned **that** further action may be taken.
She agreed with her parents and brothers **that** it would be safer to buy a car than a motorbike.
examples.note: rather than ... and brothers it would be safer ...

lesson.heading: A formal alternative: object + to-infinitive

left.label: that-clause
examples: I felt **that the results were** satisfactory.
The judge thought **that his explanation was** unconvincing.

right.label: object + to-infinitive (often to be)
right.text: Rather formal, and only after certain verbs. Also: acknowledge, assume, believe, consider, declare, expect, find, presume, report, think, understand.
examples: I felt **the results to be** satisfactory.
The judge thought **his explanation to be** unconvincing.
Houston reported **the satellite to be** missing.

lesson.note: Verbs like argue, stress and comment have no such alternative: not ~~The employees argued the reduction to be unlawful~~.

lesson.heading: Verbs that must have an object
lesson.text: After an active form of some verbs we have to put an object between the verb and the that-clause, and that object cannot be a prepositional one. Also: assure, convince, inform, persuade, reassure, remind, tell.

examples.text: I notified **the bank** that I had changed my address.
examples.wrong: I notified that I ... / I notified to the bank that I ...

examples.text: The police assured **residents** that everything possible was being done.

lesson.note: After advise, show, teach and warn the object is optional: They promised (me) that they would come to the party.

lesson.heading: Verbs that need a preposition before the object
rows: admit, announce, complain, confess, explain, indicate, mention, point out, propose, recommend, report, say, suggest
She admitted (**to me**) that she was seriously ill.
We agreed (**with Ella**) that the information should go no further.
The company demands (**of its staff**) that they should be at work by 8:30.
lesson.note: With these verbs the object can also be left out altogether: I pointed out that he had parked across the entrance.

lesson.heading: ask, demand and require
lesson.text: The pattern with **of** is formal. Less formally, ask and require can take an object + to-infinitive instead - but demand cannot.

examples.text: The club asks **of its members** that they pay their fees by 31st December.
The club asks **its members to pay** their fees by 31st December.
The company demands **of its staff** that they should be at work by 8:30.
examples.wrong: The company demands its staff to be at work

lesson.text: Before writing a that-clause, ask yourself: does this verb take a plain object (*told me*), a prepositional object (*explained to me*), or neither?

exercises.prompt: The doctors ___ that I should rest for three months.
exercises.explanation: persuade and remind must have an object before the that-clause; advise does not need one.

exercises.prompt: The police ___ residents that everything possible was being done to catch the thieves.
exercises.explanation: Both work here: assure always takes an object, and promise allows one.

exercises.prompt: Russian scientists ___ that honey can prevent the growth of bacteria.
exercises.explanation: convince and inform need an object before the that-clause; show does not.

exercises.prompt: Katarina ___ that she would be home before midnight.
exercises.explanation: tell requires an object (told me that ...), so only promise fits a sentence with no object.

exercises.prompt: Match each reporting verb with the object that can follow it.

pairs.right: the bank that I had changed my address.
to me that she was seriously ill.
with Ella that the information should go no further.
of its members that they pay their fees by 31st December.

exercises.prompt: Martina ___ the shop assistant that the laptop she'd bought there was faulty.
exercises.explanation: complain takes to before a personal object: complained to the shop assistant that ...

exercises.prompt: I ___ Mr Jacobs that the students were lazy. I thought they were very enthusiastic.
exercises.explanation: disagree takes with before the object.

exercises.prompt: The college ___ its students that they attend all classes.
exercises.explanation: ask, demand and require take of before the object in this formal pattern.

exercises.statement: Managing Director Beth Edwards explained employees that a national fall in demand for traditional toys is to blame.
exercises.explanation: ... explained to employees that a national fall in demand ... explain needs to before a personal object.

exercises.statement: PIK, the toy manufacturer, has warned that they are to make over 100 employees redundant.
exercises.explanation: Correct. warn does not need an object, and that is kept in formal writing.

exercises.prompt: Which of these verbs also allow the formal object + to-infinitive pattern (reported the satellite to be missing)?
Rewrite 'We found that the rugby supporters were very well behaved' in the more formal pattern.
exercises.answer: We found the rugby supporters to be very well behaved
exercises.explanation: find allows object + to-infinitive as a formal alternative to a that-clause.
